<reason>B better defended the proposition as written and established an incremental protective benefit where parental controls are absent. A raised legitimate implementation risks, but repeatedly treated problematic existing systems as defeating a mandate expressly conditioned on privacy preservation. B directly answered the metadata and displacement objections; A never established comparable protection from household tools or justified assuming that children without parental controls would circumvent provider checks.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s closing exposed A’s unsupported leap from missing parental supervision to guaranteed circumvention. This preserved the distinction between children whose access would be interrupted and determined evaders, undermining both A’s displacement argument and its claim that household controls were an adequate substitute.</best_rebuttal>
